headline: DEVELOPING: Manila Hospital Says ER Reached 300% Capacity Amid Leptospirosis Surge
seoTitle: Manila Hospital ER Reached 300% Capacity Amid Leptospirosis Surge | FMB News
seoDescription: Justice Jose Abad Santos General Hospital said its ER reached 300% capacity amid patient influx including suspected and confirmed leptospirosis cases.
deck: A hospital public advisory quoted by Inquirer said the emergency room reached 300% capacity amid continued patient arrivals, including suspected and confirmed leptospirosis cases.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Justice Jose Abad Santos General Hospital said in a public advisory reproduced by Inquirer that its emergency room had reached 300 percent of regular capacity amid a continued influx of patients, including suspected and confirmed leptospirosis cases.
The hospital warned that some patients could be referred to other facilities and said its outpatient department would handle non-emergency cases beginning September 1.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The hospital is a Manila city facility with 150 beds. The capacity warning came as flood-related leptospirosis cases were rising nationally and locally after prolonged heavy rain.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: Severe emergency-room crowding can affect waiting times, referrals and the ability of hospitals to absorb additional urgent cases during a disaster-related health surge.

sections.heading: What remains unclear
paragraphs: FMB News could verify that Inquirer reproduced the hospital advisory, but the current primary advisory itself was not retrievable from the hospital’s public website during this check. The 300 percent figure describes the hospital’s reported condition at the time of that advisory and should not be assumed to remain unchanged in real time.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for a newer hospital capacity advisory, Manila health updates and further DOH surveillance data on leptospirosis.
